page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-44 is a compute-focused instance within the C3 machine series, designed for computationally intensive tasks requiring a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It provides 44 dedicated vCPUs derived from 22 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, backed by an x86_64 architecture and a 105 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 88.0 GB of RAM, allocating 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached block storage for persistent data requirements.

Hardware-level vector and matrix extensions provide measurable performance advantages in cryptographic and data-processing tasks. Features like Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), AVX-512, and VAES drive strong performance in PassMark CPU encryption benchmarks and Geekbench image processing tests, ranking in the top 25 percent. The instance also shows capable CPU-based inference handling on smaller models, delivering 292.13 tokens per second on text generation with a 135M parameter model and 185.65 tokens per second on prompt processing for a 7B model. Larger language models, such as 70B parameters, demonstrate noticeable degradation during text generation due to the absence of dedicated GPU accelerators.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3-highcpu-44 delivers dense processing power and modern instruction set acceleration without the overhead of unneeded memory capacity or dedicated accelerator hardware. Workloads that align with this architectural profile include CI/CD software compilation, batch encoding, scientific simulation, cryptographic operations, and CPU-driven web or application servers that operate within the 88 GB memory boundary.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-44 is a compute-oriented virtual server engineered for high-throughput computational workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 44 dedicated vCPUs across 22 physical cores with hyper-threading, accompanied by 88.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks integrated GPUs and bundled local storage, requiring network block storage for persistence. In benchmark evaluations, the c3-highcpu-44 demonstrates top-quartile performance in CPU encryption and image processing, supported by Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions. Memory bandwidth achieves 114.34 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, while CPU-based inference remains capable on small-to-medium models but restricted on 70B parameter models. Without unneeded RAM overhead, this configuration offers solid compute density for CI/CD compilation, batch workloads, cryptography, and containerized backend microservices.
